source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Localized overgrowth of a digit with cable-like median nerve on MRI. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Macrodystrophia lipomatosa with fibrolipomatous hamartoma of the median nerve}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 964. Cable-like fatty expansion of the median nerve is the key diagnostic feature.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What do the yellow arrows indicate on the hand radiograph?

{{c1::Broadened phalanges with proliferative osseous change}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 964. This is the radiographic component of macrodystrophia lipomatosa.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What do the red arrows indicate on these MRI images?

{{c1::Expanded median nerve with cable-like fascicles}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 964. Fat interdigitating between nerve fascicles is pathognomonic for fibrolipomatous hamartoma.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Large heterogeneously enhancing thigh mass with central necrosis. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 965. Core notes this appearance overlaps with other high-grade sarcomas.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Large predominantly T2-hyperintense enhancing soft-tissue mass. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Myxofibrosarcoma}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 965. Myxoid elements make this high-grade sarcoma characteristically T2 hyperintense.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Enhancing nodular mass along the plantar aponeurosis. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Plantar fibromatosis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 966. Plantar fibromatosis is Ledderhose disease.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Rapidly growing T2-hyperintense enhancing intramuscular mass. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Nodular fasciitis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 966. Nodular fasciitis is benign but may mimic sarcoma clinically and on imaging.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Crescentic infrascapular mass deep to latissimus dorsi with alternating fatty striations. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Elastofibroma dorsi}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 967. The subscapular location deep to latissimus dorsi and alternating fibrous-fatty striations are the key pattern.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Multiple low-signal interfascial lesions with patchy enhancement. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Desmoid fibromatosis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 967. Desmoid fibromatosis is benign but locally aggressive and is associated with Gardner syndrome.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Lobulated enhancing cutaneous abdominal wall mass. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 967. DFSP is a slowly growing intermediate-grade cutaneous malignancy.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Circumscribed enhancing T2-hyperintense mass eccentric to a peripheral nerve. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Schwannoma}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 968. Schwannoma may be eccentric and separable from the nerve, unlike a neurofibroma that expands the nerve centrally.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the red arrow indicate?

{{c1::Tibial nerve splayed eccentrically around the mass}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 968. Eccentric relationship to the nerve supports schwannoma.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Patient with NF1 and a large enhancing T2-hyperintense mass arising from the tibial nerve. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 969. A new or enlarging mass in NF1 should raise concern for MPNST.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the blue arrow indicate?

{{c1::Target sign}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 969. The target sign supports a neurogenic tumor but does not prove benignity.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the green arrow indicate?

{{c1::Split fat sign}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 969. The split fat sign is a preserved fat triangle at the margin of a neurogenic tumor.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Near-fluid signal intramuscular mass with faint wispy enhancement. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Myxoma}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 970. Myxoid matrix produces near-fluid signal with minimal enhancement.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Young patient with a T2-hyperintense enhancing mass near the wrist that does not simply behave like a ganglion. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Synovial sarcoma}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 970. Synovial sarcoma is often near joints but does not arise from synovium.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the red arrow indicate?

{{c1::Internal complexity within the near-fluid signal mass}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 970. Internal complexity helps separate synovial sarcoma from a simple cyst or ganglion.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Dumbbell-shaped enhancing mass in the plantar second interspace. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Morton neuroma}}

1/2
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 971. Morton neuroma is perineural fibrosis rather than a true nerve neoplasm.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
This schematic illustrates development of characteristic lesions in what process?

{{c1::Osteomyelitis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 974. The diagram shows progression from acute hematogenous osteomyelitis to Brodie abscess and chronic osteomyelitis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Which age group can hematogenous osteomyelitis spread across the physis through bridging vessels?

{{c1::Infants up to 12 months}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 975. In infants, bridging vessels can allow metaphyseal infection to involve the epiphysis and joint.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Diabetic patient with diffuse midfoot edema but no ulcer or sinus tract. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Charcot arthropathy}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 976. Charcot arthropathy usually involves the midfoot and lacks a contiguous ulcer or sinus tract.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Lytic metaphyseal lesion with surrounding sclerosis and soft-tissue swelling. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Brodie abscess}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 977. Brodie abscess is a walled-off intraosseous abscess of subacute osteomyelitis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Heel pad abscess contiguous with calcaneal marrow edema and cortical irregularity. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Calcaneal osteomyelitis}}

1/4
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 978. Contiguous soft-tissue infection with cortical disruption and T1 marrow replacement supports osteomyelitis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Which T1 marrow pattern is shown?

{{c1::Confluent intramedullary signal change}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 979. Confluent intramedullary T1 marrow replacement is strongly associated with osteomyelitis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Which T1 marrow pattern is shown?

{{c1::Hazy reticular signal change}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 979. Hazy reticular T1 signal does not reliably diagnose osteomyelitis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Which T1 marrow pattern is shown?

{{c1::Subcortical signal change}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 979. A thin subcortical T1 signal change is not associated with osteomyelitis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Soft-tissue gas in the medial thigh on CT. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Necrotizing fasciitis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 980. Gas bubbles in soft tissues on radiograph or CT are the characteristic imaging clue.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the arrow indicate?

{{c1::Tiny locules of soft-tissue gas}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 980. Soft-tissue gas in the right clinical setting is a surgical emergency.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Irregular low-attenuation collection within the quadriceps muscle. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Pyomyositis with abscess}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 980. Pyomyositis is bacterial infection of muscle, most commonly Staphylococcus aureus.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the arrow indicate?

{{c1::Looser zone}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 982. A Looser zone is a cortical pseudofracture highly specific for osteomalacia.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Hand subperiosteal resorption and salt-and-pepper skull. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Hyperparathyroidism}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 983. Subperiosteal resorption along the radial aspects of the second and third middle phalanges is specific.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What do the arrows indicate on the hand radiograph?

{{c1::Subperiosteal resorption}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 983. Radial-sided subperiosteal resorption of the second and third middle phalanges is classic for hyperparathyroidism.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Symmetric vertebral endplate sclerosis in renal failure. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Renal osteodystrophy}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 984. Rugger jersey spine reflects secondary hyperparathyroidism and abnormal vitamin D metabolism in chronic renal failure.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
What does the arrow indicate?

{{c1::Short fourth metacarpal}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 984. Short fourth or fifth metacarpal is the classic radiographic finding of pseudohypoparathyroidism and pseudo-pseudohypoparathyroidism.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Patchy cloud-like calvarial sclerosis with thickened calvarium. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Mixed-phase Paget disease}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 985. Cotton wool skull is classic for mixed-phase Paget disease.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Peripheral cortical thickening of a vertebral body. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Picture frame vertebral body from Paget disease}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 986. Unlike rugger jersey spine, picture frame vertebra involves the periphery of the vertebral body.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Asymmetric pelvic cortical and trabecular thickening. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Paget disease of the pelvis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 986. Paget disease of the pelvis produces asymmetric coarsened trabeculae and thickened iliopectineal or ilioischial lines.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Flame-shaped lytic margin progressing distally in a long bone. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Lytic-phase Paget disease}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 986. The blade-of-grass margin helps distinguish Paget disease from neoplasm.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Diffuse dramatic skeletal sclerosis with brittle-bone fracture. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Osteopetrosis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 987. Osteopetrosis causes diffuse marked sclerosis because osteoclasts cannot resorb bone normally.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Central endplate depressions of vertebral bodies in sickle cell disease. What named appearance is shown?

{{c1::H-shaped vertebral bodies}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 988. H-shaped vertebral bodies reflect vertebral endplate avascular necrosis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Sickle cell patient with flattened sclerotic femoral heads. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Bilateral femoral head avascular necrosis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 988. Femoral heads are common sites of infarction in sickle cell disease.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Older patient with splenomegaly and diffusely dense bones. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Myelofibrosis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 989. Progressive marrow fibrosis leads to anemia, splenomegaly, and diffuse skeletal sclerosis.

Full source page:

source_title: Core Radiology 2nd ed. MSK visual cards, macrodystrophia through hematologic disease

fields.Text:
Coronal CT images showing diffuse and patchy skeletal sclerosis in two patients. Most likely diagnosis?

{{c1::Mastocytosis}}
fields.Extra:
Core Radiology 2nd ed., MSK: 989. Mastocytosis can produce diffuse or patchy sclerosis from marrow reaction to infiltrating mast cells.

Full source page:
